rows.ARS:
Red blend Floribunda.
Registration name: JELroganor
rows.Origin:
Bred by Robert G. Jelly (United States, 1968).
Introduced in United States by Conard-Pyle (Star Roses) in 1977 as 'Charisma'.
rows.Bloom: Red and yellow. Mild fragrance. 35 to 50 petals. Average diameter 1.75". Small to medium, full (26-40 petals), cluster-flowered, in small clusters, high-centered to cupped bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season.
rows.Habit: Bushy, well-branched. Glossy, leathery foliage. 7 leaflets.
rows.Growing: USDA zone 6b and warmer. Heat tolerant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) . Can be grown in the ground or in a container (container requires winter protection).
rows.Patents:

rows.Notes: Tate Rose Nursery says this rose has masses of bright, eye-catching blooms of scarlet and gold which age mostly to red...
